Note::TexAccessor::sup_norm¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::sup_norm() const

Brace Every Bare Superscript¶

sup_norm() wraps every unbraced superscript — ^x, a run of one or more ASCII letters/digits, or ^\alpha, a single control word — in explicit braces: ^{x}, ^{\alpha}. It is the exact ^ counterpart of sub_norm; every rule there — the greedy alnum run, the untouched already-braced form, the whole-word control-word capture — applies identically here with ^ in place of _.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Undefined input remains undefined; Bool, Int64, Float64, and Bytes receivers are rejected because TeX source is Text.

Example 1: Bare, Control-Word, And Already-Braced Forms¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"x^2 + y^ab + z^\\alpha + w^{already}"})
              .tex().sup_norm()
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["x^{2} + y^{ab} + z^{\\alpha} + w^{already}"]

Example 2: The Greedy Run Captures Digit And Letter Together¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"a^1b^2", "no sups here"})
              .tex().sup_norm()
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["a^{1b}^{2}", "no sups here"]

Exactly the same greedy-run behavior documented on sub_norm applies here: 1b is captured as one superscript, not split at the digit.

Example 3: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().sup_norm().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().sup_norm();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • sub_norm: the identical bracing rule applied to _ instead of ^.

  • prime_norm: rewrites trailing ' marks into an explicit ^{...} superscript.
